explorationReceipt.approximateInspectedScope: Approximately 58 named tracks and releases across ten official release, retailer, catalogue and bounded-query windows; metadata/text review only and zero audio auditions.
exclusions: All 12 canonical identities, active placement-specific rejections and every untriggered PARKED revisit were excluded. Run 46 material was not recycled.
The protected Transparency → When We Froze → Stardancer internal order and its two protected handoffs remain untouched; the proposed new track follows the intact block.

DBX002 supplied exact current-release descriptions, but Funchal and its Alexander Kowalski remix emphasized atmospheric driving depth and warmth without enough track-specific rhythmic or structural evidence for this run; no identity was invented.
Orlando Voorn's Maneuvers In Space supplied current exact identity, date and tags only; weird/electro/Detroit tags do not establish behavior or placement.

Marcal's Smoke From Respawn and Arapuca supplied unusually strong exact-track rhythmic descriptions, but the EP remains a 2026-09-11 preorder. They were retained as a release watch rather than padded into current canonical resolution.
Stefan Vincent's Soothing the Beast supplied exact polyrhythmic acid and halftime-break language, but its 2026-09-18 preorder status makes it a watch, not a current canonical lead.
Retter's Palindro and Rhizome supplied useful release-level broken-rhythm and percussion framing without enough exact-track placement evidence for this request.
Transhuman supplied broken-rhythm, spacious-arrangement, dub and techno framing only at EP level; no exact track was promoted from that shared description.
No lead was admitted for recency, BPM, genre tag, title, artist reputation, novelty or quota completion. Unknown energy, density, phrase structure, perceived pulse and mixability remain unknown.

leads.fitHypothesis: Vakuum Label describes DT229 specifically as closing the record by diving into broken rhythms and more melodic spheres. That supports the volume's broad rhythmic/structural-freedom lens and suggests a deliberate post-trio left turn, but it does not establish the perceived Stardancer handoff, energy relation, phrase fit or long-form success.

evidence.attributedDescription: Vakuum Label says DT229 closes the EP by diving into broken rhythms and more melodic spheres. This is label language, not heard or measured behavior.
evidence.listenerEvidence: The user positively reports the protected three-track block through Stardancer as being in perfect harmony. No report covers the outgoing Stardancer → DT229 handoff.
evidence.craftConvention: After a listener-confirmed block, a concise and conspicuous change of rhythmic character can open a new passage when it feels intentional; contrast itself is not proof.
evidence.editorialInterpretation: Potential post-trio afterword and doorway into a more broken vocabulary, with transition and long-form effect still to be evaluated.
